notes: Measured on main d0d276a86705aac965d23a8a9c462c6103b38f52 (grit 0.6.0, release build, nothing changed in the code) with one full `grit-bench daily --http-server target/release/grit-http-server` invocation (default warmups and min-runs, all 172 scenarios) on a 4-vCPU VM (Intel Xeon, 15.6 GiB, ext4 scratch); grit is compared with git version 2.43.0 only (no baseline release). hyperfine 2.0.0 was installed with cargo; libkrb5-dev/libclang-dev/clang were installed so grit-cli builds (libgssapi-sys). A first invocation started 2026-11-27 23:07 UTC with a cold fixture cache (git.git v2.47.0 clone, deep-history and history-rewrite sources were generated) and aborted at the clone/http@synth-10k setup because grit-http-server had not been built; it produced no data. After building grit-http-server the full run was repeated against the warm cache: it started 2026-11-28 00:06 UTC and ended about 01:15 UTC (the report `timestamp` is that run's start; `date` is the task day 2026-11-27). All 172 scenarios completed for both tools: no failures, none skipped. Conversion from grit-bench's raw JSON: median_wall_ms -> median_ms, peak_rss_bytes -> max_rss_kb (bytes/1024, floored), id split into command/case/repo, scenario `detail` and per-tool runs/samples_ms/min_ms/max_ms/stddev_ms carried over unchanged. area keeps grit-bench's native area names, as in previous reports. The repos table is carried over from the previous report (same pinned fixtures, git.git v2.47.0) because grit-bench daily does not emit one. grit-bench flags a different set of rows as headline than the task table (it also flags e.g. branch/list-json, branch/merged, log/json-100, pull/rebase, push/force-with-lease); this report marks exactly the 17 scenarios in the headline table. Noise check against the 2026-11-26 report: three scenarios crossed a re-run threshold (grit/git time ratio >20% worse): branch/contains-json@git-git-10k-refs (1.25x), branch/contains@git-git-10k-refs (1.31x) and status/paths@synth-100k (1.29x). Each was re-run three more times (grit-bench daily --offline --only <ids>); runs/samples_ms/min/max/stddev pool all 4 invocations, median_ms is the median of all pooled samples and max_rss_kb the median of the 4 per-invocation peaks. After pooling, status/paths@synth-100k is back within threshold (grit/git 0.95 vs 0.88 before, 1.07x). branch/contains-json and branch/contains@git-git-10k-refs stay above it (grit/git ratio 1.25x and 1.36x of the previous report's): grit now takes ~31-33 ms (previous report ~24-25 ms) while git takes ~29.7 s (the ratio is ~0.001 either way), so the regression is a ~7-9 ms absolute change that was reproducible across all 4 invocations. No scenario exceeded the 30% memory-ratio threshold. Sub-3 ms rows (git ~1-2 ms) are dominated by process start-up, so their ratios are coarse.
